title: Mini Writing Practice: Explain and Persuade
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: This short, unofficial classroom practice gives students a test-like writing routine. Students complete one paragraph-ordering task, one sentence-completion task, and two short constructed-response writing prompts. Frames and word banks support multilingual learners while keeping the writing demand at a Grades 6-8 level.

sections.title: Part 1: Build and Complete
sections.directions: Read each item carefully. For the ordering item, put the sentences in order. For the cloze item, choose the best word for each blank.

items.title: Order the Informational Paragraph
vocabulary: the sentence that names the main idea
oración temática: la oración que nombra la idea principal
secuencia: el orden de los pasos
items.prompt: Put the sentences in order to build a clear paragraph about studying for a test.

items.text: Studying for a test works best with a simple plan.
First, you review your notes from class.
Next, you practice with a few sample questions.
Finally, you get a good night of sleep before the test.

items.correct: Correct. The topic sentence comes first, then the steps in order, ending with the final step.
items.hint: Find the sentence that names the topic, then follow First, Next, and Finally.
items.support: A paragraph begins with a topic sentence and uses sequence words to stay in order.
items.extension: Add one more study step using the word then.

items.title: Complete the Opinion Sentence
items.skill: Choose the best word to complete a sentence
vocabulary: opinión: lo que piensas o sientes
the word that gives a reason
porque: la palabra que da una razón
items.prompt: Choose the best word for each blank.
items.correct: Correct. Helpful states the opinion, and because gives the reason.
items.hint: Which word names a positive opinion? Which word signals a reason?
items.support: An opinion sentence often pairs a describing word with because and a reason.
items.extension: Write your own opinion sentence using because.

sections.title: Part 2: Write Your Response
sections.directions: Read each prompt. Write a complete response. Use the frames and word bank to help you. Check your work when you finish.

items.title: Short Opinion Paragraph
items.skill: Write a short opinion paragraph with reasons
vocabulary: opinión: lo que piensas o sientes
frames: One reason is ___. Another reason is ___.
items.prompt: Prompt: Should students choose their own seats in class? Write your opinion and give two reasons. Try to write at least 40 words.
items.responsePlaceholder: In my opinion, ___ . One reason is ___ . Another reason is ___ .
items.correct: Strong response: In my opinion, students should choose their own seats. One reason is that students focus better next to people who help them work. Another reason is that choosing a seat teaches responsibility because students must make a good choice.
items.hint: State your opinion first, then give two reasons using because.
items.support: Model: In my opinion, recess should be longer. One reason is that exercise helps us learn. Another reason is that fresh air relaxes us.
items.extension: Add a closing sentence that restates your opinion.

items.title: Persuasive Note to a Teacher
items.skill: Write a short persuasive note with a polite request
vocabulary: to make someone agree with you
persuadir: hacer que alguien esté de acuerdo
frames: I would like to request ___ because ___.
Thank you for considering this. Sincerely, ___
items.prompt: Prompt: Write a short note asking your teacher for extra time on an assignment. Give one clear reason. Try to write at least 30 words.
items.responsePlaceholder: Dear ___, I would like to request ___ because ___. Thank you for considering this. Sincerely, ___
items.correct: Strong response: Dear Ms. Patel, I would like to request two more days on the essay because I was sick this week and missed class. Thank you for considering this. Sincerely, Leo.
items.hint: Start with Dear, make a polite request with because, and end with Sincerely.
items.support: Model: Dear Mr. Kim, I would like to request extra time because my computer broke. Thank you for considering this. Sincerely, Ava.
items.extension: Add one sentence offering a plan to finish the work.
